panels.title: Rate / Errors / Duration — every latency panel sliced by route (R30)
Request rate by route and outcome
panels.description: R (rate). Split by outcome so an error spike is visible as a shape change, not only in the errors panel.

panels.title: Error ratio by route
panels.description: E (errors). A ratio, not a count -- a count rises with traffic and says nothing on its own. The `or ... * 0` is load-bearing and was found by running this live: with zero errors the {outcome=~"error|empty"} series does not EXIST, so the division returns no result and the panel reads "No data" instead of 0%. clamp_min guards the denominator; nothing but the `or` guards a missing numerator.

targets.expr: (sum by (route) (rate(mitya_request_duration_seconds_count{outcome=~"error|empty"}[5m])) or sum by (route) (rate(mitya_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) * 0) / clamp_min(sum by (route) (rate(mitya_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])), 1e-9)

panels.title: TTFT p95 by route
panels.description: D (duration). SLICED BY ROUTE, and that is not cosmetic: R30 measured DEFAULT 7.790s against STRUCTURAL 4.260s, so a single unsliced p95 is a statement about the traffic mix rather than about the system.

panels.title: Stage p95 by stage and route
panels.description: Where the time actually goes. Rerank was measured at 84% of the retrieval path (~2.24s) and is the largest standing item in the phase.

panels.title: Spend — read the provisional counters beside every total (G5)
Metered spend (window)
panels.description: PROVISIONAL unless the two counters to the right are both zero. Charter G5: any aggregate containing an unmetered or unpriced answer is reported provisional, never as a cost. This figure is the sum of the answers we could actually price — it is NOT the cost of serving the window.

panels.title: Unmetered answers (window)
panels.description: Nothing bills us for these — local inference on hardware we own. Non-zero makes the total to the left provisional. Reporting these as $0.00 would be false; reporting them as unmetered is exactly true.

panels.title: Unpriced answers (window)
panels.description: Somebody billed us and we cannot say how much — a model with no rate row. Distinct from unmetered, and worse: it is a gap in the table, not a fact about the hardware. Non-zero means add the row to MODEL_RATES.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio by route (memory-free population only)
panels.description: A5's saving claim is measured here. A hit generates nothing, so it bills nothing -- this is cost avoided, and it becomes a dollar figure the moment P2 meters anything. Same `or ... * 0` as the error panel: with zero hits the numerator series is absent entirely and the panel would read "No data" rather than 0%. **v2 P6 step 7(b), G-P12(b): this ratio is over the MEMORY-FREE population only.** Memory-bearing requests bypass the cache entirely and are counted on `mitya_cache_bypassed_total`, a separate metric name, so they can never enter this denominator by accident. Read it beside "Memory-bearing bypass share": a rising bypass share with a flat ratio is adoption, not degradation, and the two are never pooled.

targets.expr: (sum by (route) (rate(mitya_cache_lookups_total{outcome="hit"}[5m])) or sum by (route) (rate(mitya_cache_lookups_total[5m])) * 0) / clamp_min(sum by (route) (rate(mitya_cache_lookups_total[5m])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Memory-bearing bypass share by route
panels.description: The other population (v2 P6 step 7(b)). Share of /chat requests that carried memory and therefore never consulted the cache. This is the ADOPTION curve: as it rises the cache serves less traffic, which is a different fact from the cache hitting less often. Pooling the two -- putting bypasses in the hit-rate denominator -- would publish adoption as cache degradation.

targets.expr: (sum by (route) (rate(mitya_cache_bypassed_total[5m])) or sum by (route) (rate(mitya_cache_lookups_total[5m])) * 0) / clamp_min(sum by (route) (rate(mitya_cache_bypassed_total[5m])) + sum by (route) (rate(mitya_cache_lookups_total[5m])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Empty completions and quota rejections
panels.description: Empty = every EMPTY_RETRIES attempt came back with no token (measured residual ~2.0% at EMPTY_RETRIES=4). Quota has no live call site on /chat at P1 — it is the offline teacher/judge path today, and the panel is here for P2's gateway.
